desc:
You are given a list words of different words, all of the same length L. Every word is an array of letter codes (1 is a, ..., 26 is z).

A word square is a sequence of L words w0, w1, ..., wL-1 taken from the list (the same word may be used several times) such that, written as the rows of an L x L grid, row k and column k read the same word for every k. In other words wi[j] = wj[i] for all i, j.

Return the number of word squares. Different sequences count as different squares, even if they hold the same words in another order. It is guaranteed that the answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.

For example, for the words ab, ba, aa there are 5 squares: (ab, ba), (ba, ab), (ba, aa), (aa, ab) and (aa, aa).
constraints: 1 ≤ L ≤ 5, all words have the same length L and are pairwise different
The answer is at most 2<sup>31</sup> - 1 and the tests keep it small enough to enumerate
hints: Fill the square one row at a time. How much freedom does row k have once rows 0..k-1 are fixed?
Column k must equal row k. The first k letters of row k are therefore already known: they are the letters at position k of the earlier rows. Row k must be a word that starts with that prefix.

Precompute a map from every prefix (as a tuple of codes, including the empty prefix) to the list of words that begin with it. The DFS asks the map for the candidates of the next row, recurses, and adds up the results.
editorial: After choosing rows 0..k-1 the prefix of row k is forced: its j-th letter must equal letter k of row j. So the choice of row k is limited to the words with that prefix. A dictionary from prefix tuples to word lists (or a trie that stores a list at every node) gives these candidates instantly, and the DFS never builds a row that already contradicts the earlier ones.

The count is the number of leaves of this search tree, and the work is proportional to the number of partial squares that can still be extended by looking at one row. Without the prefix map, scanning the whole list for each row would multiply the cost by the number of words. Memory is O(number of words · L) for the map.
